goal: Replace Chickenbro's fixed source Tool selection with a PostgreSQL-backed immutable Tool Registry Release while preserving answer, evidence, owner and source boundaries.
userValue: Players keep asking natural-language questions while the service can prove which released source capabilities were available, discovered and selected without opening an arbitrary-code or self-publishing path.
scope: immutable PostgreSQL Tool manifests and active Registry Release
deterministic Registry discovery for existing Raider.IO and Warcraft Logs Tools
repository-bound adapter execution with no arbitrary implementation loading
Registry Trace v2 with P1 Trace v1 read compatibility
read-only Registry health and bounded verified-cache degradation
outOfScope: new Tools or wrapping personal template and SimC context as Tools
Cloud Codex Toolsmith or candidate generation
shadow, canary, promotion or model training
frontend, public response schema or answer-policy changes
nonGoals: Do not add new Tools or register personal template and SimC context as Tools.
Do not add CapabilityGap persistence, Cloud Codex Toolsmith, candidate generation, shadow, canary, promotion or model training.
Do not allow manifests, models or clients to select arbitrary implementations, code, URLs, credentials or owner values.
Do not change the frontend, public response schema or answer policy.

mustChange: Create immutable PostgreSQL Registry manifests, releases, membership and one separately mutable active pointer.
Discover exactly the existing Raider.IO and Warcraft Logs capabilities from a verified active release.
Execute only repository-bound adapters and expose bounded Registry identity in Trace v2 and health.
Fail closed without the old fixed allowlist when Registry identity is unavailable, invalid or expired.
mustNotChange: The initial Registry contains exactly source:raiderio:v1 and source:warcraftlogs:v1.
Personal templates and SimC remain context evidence rather than Tools.
No arbitrary implementation, code, URL, credential or owner input becomes executable.
Existing public response schema, frontend and answer policy remain unchanged.
Phase 3-5 persistence, generation and promotion surfaces remain absent.
riskUnknown: Candidate PostgreSQL privilege behavior, bounded cache degradation and production script-entrypoint wiring require cloud proof.
Additive Registry tables remain after code rollback and must not affect the restored P1 fixed-allowlist runtime.
evidenceRequired: Migration and Ops-store contract tests with immutable rows and read-only wow_app privileges.
Focused Registry, runtime, Trace v2, Eval and backend regression tests.
Local CR and exact clean-HEAD full Harness verification.
Candidate three-path smoke, isolated failure probes, exact health and owner-isolated Trace reads.
Code rollback to P1 and exact P2 candidate restoration with service, hash and timer/backflow evidence.

ownership.factOwner: server/chickenbro_registry.py owns immutable Registry validation and discovery; server/chickenbro_tool_runtime.py owns verified cache and approved adapter dispatch; server/postgres_ops_store.py owns the transactional active-release read; server/news_backend.py only orchestrates the request path.

engineeringHealth.reason: The request-path seam remains in news_backend, but schema validation, discovery, verified caching and adapter dispatch are isolated pure modules; PostgreSQL runtime access is read-only and failures are explicit and fail closed.

acceptanceEvidence: Exactly two deterministic manifest identities are loaded behind one active immutable release and wow_app cannot write Registry state.
Build, public WCL and general questions preserve existing public responses while Trace v2 separates discovered and selected capabilities.
Unavailable, invalid and expired Registry probes do not call the fixed allowlist or an unregistered adapter.
Historical Trace v1 remains readable while new Registry-backed requests write Trace v2.
The exact clean candidate passes full Harness, candidate cloud smoke and P1 code rollback/restoration.

decisionLog.decision: The user approved a dynamic capability mechanism rather than a static public knowledge base.
The user authorized Phase 2 completion with exactly the two existing source Tools; Phase 3-5 remain separately gated.
